title: How faith concurs: instrumental, relative/objective, or covenant condition
source_text: XXI. Porro qui sunt in hac sententia, non eodem modo explicant qua ratione hic fides interveniat, & concurrat ad peccatoris justificationem. Nam hic varii varie loquuntur. Plurimi dicunt fidem justificare, quoniam est nostrae justificationis causa instrumentalis, per quam Christi justitia Evangelii verbo oblata accipitur, & nobis applicatur, in remissionem peccatorum nostrorum. Nec alia videtur esse mens eorum qui docent fidem justificare relative sive objective. Per hoc enim aliud significatum volunt, nisi quod fides propria virtute non justificat, sed solummodo quatenus apprehendit Christi meritum & obedientiam, per quam solam proprie coram Deo justificamur. Alii dicere malunt fidem justificare quoniam est conditio quam foedus gratiae, sive Evangelium, postulat a nobis ut justificemur. Siquidem remissionem peccatorum in Christi sanguine, & vitam aeternam omni credenti offert.
pass_a_gloss: Further, those who hold this view do not explain in the same way by what reason faith here intervenes and concurs toward the sinner's justification. For here various people speak variously. Most say faith justifies because it is the instrumental cause of our justification, through which Christ's righteousness offered by the word of the Gospel is received and applied to us for the remission of our sins. Nor does any other seem to be the mind of those who teach that faith justifies relatively or objectively. For by this they want no other meaning than that faith does not justify by its own virtue, but only insofar as it apprehends Christ's merit and obedience, by which alone we are properly justified before God. Others prefer to say faith justifies because it is the condition that the covenant of grace, or the Gospel, requires of us that we may be justified—since it offers remission of sins in Christ's blood and eternal life to every believer.
pass_b_english: Most: faith is the instrumental cause receiving Christ's offered righteousness.
Others: relative/objective apprehension; others: gospel covenant condition.

choices.english: condition of the covenant of grace
